pk.context: 1000 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Less than 15% of an oral dose is absorbed as parent drug, and it is over 99.3% bound to albumin. Intestinal bacteria break it down, and its products are mainly eliminated in the urine.
clues.substance: The parent compound has a molecular weight of 398.4 and is an azo compound of salicylic acid.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 500 mg tablets, with a delayed-release form also listed.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in intestinal or urinary obstruction, porphyria, and hypersensitivity to sulfonamides or salicylates; nausea and headache are among the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Mild to moderate ulcerative colitis, adjunctive therapy in severe cases, and prolonging remission between acute attacks.
clues.mechanism: Classed as an anti-inflammatory agent, it is split by intestinal bacteria, and most of its 5-aminosalicylic acid part stays in the colon.

tell: Gut bacteria split this 1950 anti-inflammatory into two products, one of which is much less well absorbed.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: Maximum concentrations of SSZ occur between 3 and 12 hours post-ingestion, with the mean peak concentration (6 µg/mL) occurring at 6 hours
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The observed plasma half-life for intravenous sulfasalazine is 7.6 ± 3.4 hours
evidence.pk.cmax: mean peak concentration (6 µg/mL) occurring at 6 hours
